incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 created — high tail latency affecting single-tenant customer Citrine Labs. Alerting p99 > 3s for streaming responses.

Ava (oncall): noticed p95 jump at ~12:07 UTC, p99 ~3.2s and streaming stalls reported. Paging eng-sre.

Jordan (eng-sre): on it. which pool/region?

Ava (oncall): customer tenant id citrine-prod-01, routed to us-east-1/gpu-pool-b. Recent deploy earlier today (deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T09:50Z).

Samir (eng-runtime): grabbing metrics. initial glance: sustained concurrency from this tenant spiked to ~1.6k concurrent sessions. KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% to 14% in last 8m.

Maria (support): Citrine is saying generation stalls at token ~512 for streaming sessions, they see `ERR_STREAM_TIMEOUT` in client.

Jordan (eng-sre): can you dump tail logs from the serving nodes for that tenant?

Samir (eng-runtime): running query: ```sql
select timestamp, latency_ms, stream_chunk_delay_ms from token_metrics where tenant='citrine-prod-01' and timestamp > now()-15m;
```

Samir (eng-runtime): results: p95 ~980ms -> 1200ms -> p99 jumps to 3.2s at 12:07. stream_chunk_delay median 60ms but 99th 2.8s.

Ava (oncall): diagnostics: any correlation with long prefixes / unusual prompts? Citrine does batch diagnostics for longprompt test yesterday.

Nate (customer-success): Citrine confirmed they rolled an upload of a large prompt template new/assistant.json around 09:30Z and started stress-testing via internal load tests at ~11:50Z. They thought it was throttled but might have increased concurrency.

Jordan (eng-sre): sounds like two factors: unusual prompt shapes (very long multi-line delimiters) causing KV caching to miss, plus high concurrency saturating batch slots leading to tail queues.

Samir (eng-runtime): checked kernel/queue metrics: batch queue length spiked to 2400 tokens waiting, avg CPU on host nodes 93%, GPU util still moderate but token scheduler latency increases with long prefixes.

Ava (oncall): immediate mitigation options?

Samir (eng-runtime): short-term: 1) enable tenant-level rate limit at 200 rps to dampen load 2) route tenant to fallback model variant `redwood-7b-quant` on separate pool for lower memory/throughput footprint 3) temporarily disable streaming chunking for this tenant (serve non-streamed responses) so we avoid chunk stall retries.

Jordan (eng-sre): also increase KV cache TTL for frequently seen prefixes for this tenant to try to recover hit rate. Might need cache warm for a few mins.

Ava (oncall): can we do 1+2 quickly?

Samir (eng-runtime): applying rate-limit now: `rdctl tenant rate-limit set citrine-prod-01 200rps` — done.

deploy-bot: route update applied to citrine-prod-01 -> fallback pool `cpu-fallback-us-east-2` (change-id: route-9876).

Samir (eng-runtime): routing to fallback model variant now. switching streaming off for that tenant: `rdctl tenant streaming disable citrine-prod-01` — done.

Maria (support): told Citrine support contact to expect degraded throughput but more stable responses. They acknowledged and asked for ETA.

Jordan (eng-sre): monitoring. initial telemetry after mitigation: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s within 90s, stream_chunk_delay 99th -> 220ms but streaming off so that metric less relevant. KV cache hit remained low ~20% but improving.

Nate (customer-success): Citrine wants guidance to avoid this in future. They were running synthetic multi-line JSON prompts with randomization which broke our canonicalization rules.

Samir (eng-runtime): root cause summary (working): high concurrency combined with prompt canonicalization mismatch causing cache misses; long prefixes cause batches to be sized differently leading to queue imbalance and tail latency for streaming sessions. New deploy earlier changed a small canonicalization tweak which widened cache keys for multi-line inputs — exacerbated cache churn.

Jordan (eng-sre): next actions: - revert canonicalization tweak for the tenant (or provide mapping whitelist) - propose dedicated capacity for Citrine if they need burst to 1k+ concurrency - add guardrail in router to detect sudden single-tenant bursts and auto-enable fallback.

Ava (oncall): who's owning revert?

Samir (eng-runtime): I can push a revert for the canonicalization change scoped to this tenant: `svc-config revert canonicalization:v2026-03-15 --scope tenant=citrine-prod-01` — queued, applying now.

deploy-bot: config revert applied (change-id: cfgrev-4532).

Samir (eng-runtime): revert confirmed. Re-checking cache hit after revert: increased to 58% within 2m. p99 now 480ms.

Jordan (eng-sre): great. Recommend we keep rate limit (200rps) and non-streaming enforced for 10m, then gradual relax while we watch. Also open post-incident ticket to analyze queueing model for long prefixes.

Ava (oncall): oncall handoff in 25m. I'll leave monitoring and make a short incident summary for the handoff channel.

Maria (support): documented customer communications: informed Citrine of mitigations (rate limit, fallback, revert) and offered dedicated capacity trial. Customer OK with current state.

Nate (customer-success): schedule follow-up with Citrine SRE/eng for prompts canonicalization best practices and recommend gating large-scale internal load tests on a staging tenant.

incident-bot: SEV2 -> Postmortem required within 72h. Add assignees: Samir (runtime), Jordan (eng-sre), Maria (support).

Ava (oncall): tl;dr for handoff: Citrine spike -> KV cache miss + long-prefix batch imbalance -> p99 spikes + streaming stalls -> mitigations: tenant rate-limit, route to fallback model, disable streaming, revert canonicalization tweak. System stable; p99 ~480ms; keeping mitigations in place for 10m then gradual relax.

Jordan (eng-sre): leaving logs/queries in #eng-sre-runbook and will attach dashboard snapshots.

Ava (oncall): handing to Samir for overnight watch. Samir?

Samir (eng-runtime): I got it. Will watch until next handoff and coordinate follow-up actions.

Ava (oncall): thanks team :thumbsup:

Maria (support): closing ticket with customer for now, will keep open until postmortem completed.

incident-bot: SEV2 status -> mitigated.
